title: Operational contract PRD for conditional latency SLOs and staged rollout gates
text:
Operational contract PRD for conditional latency SLOs and staged rollout gates

description:
PRD to define conditional latency SLOs (by request class), availability targets, error budget policies, and automated staged-rollout gates for model and runtime changes. This document captures requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout phasing, and monitoring needed to land an operational contract that can be enforced by CI/CD pipelines and the Console rollout engine.

background:
Current deployments use single aggregated latency bands that do not reflect diverse request classes (interactive chat, streaming, background embeddings). This causes noisy rollouts: a change that improves batch throughput can accidentally violate interactive latency targets during traffic spikes. We need conditional SLOs and deterministic rollout gates so product teams can safely deploy runtime and model changes with predictable user impact.

goals:
Define per-request-class SLOs (interactive, streaming, embeddings, batch) with percentile targets and error budgets
Specify automated staged-rollout gating conditions (canary -> ramp -> full) driven by SLO and error-budget signals
Integrate gating checks into deployment pipelines and Console rollout UI so rollouts can be paused/rolled back automatically
Provide monitoring dashboards and alerting for SLO burn, gateways, and degradation actions
Document acceptance criteria and runbooks for on-call response to automated gate triggers

non_goals:
This PRD does not change pricing or billing models
Does not introduce new model architectures or kernel selections; focuses on operational controls
Does not build a per-tenant SLA legal agreement (that is a separate legal/commercial task)

requirements:
R1: Define request-class taxonomy and mapping rules (interactive | streaming | embeddings | batch)
R2: For each class, define p50/p95/p99 latency targets and an availability target (monthly window)
R3: Define error budget windows (rolling 30d and 7d) and burn-rate calculation method
R4: Implement rollout gate checks that evaluate: error-budget burn-rate, p95 latency, availability, and error rate over the canary window
R5: Rollout engine must support automatic rollback and controlled ramp percentages (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) and pause if gate fails
R6: Expose per-model and per-route SLO dashboards in Console with drilldown to tenant-level where applicable
R7: Create synthetic and replay traffic tests in CI that emulate each request class and produce pass/fail signals for gates
R8: Provide runbook steps and PagerDuty escalation mapping for SLO breaches and automated rollback events

slo_definitions:
Interactive (ui-chat): p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 450ms, availability >= 99.95% (30-day window)
Streaming (server-side streaming): p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms, availability >= 99.9%
Embeddings (single-call): p95 <= 800ms, p99 <= 1500ms, availability >= 99.9%
Batch (bulk/async): p95 <= 2000ms, p99 <= 5000ms, availability >= 99.5%

error_budget_policy:
Error budget = (1 - availability_target) over 30d rolling window
Burn-rate calculated as error_budget_consumed / expected_budget for same window; critical threshold when burn-rate > 4 for the 1h window or > 1.5 sustained over 3h
If error budget consumed > 50% in 7d window, restrict non-critical rollouts to conservative ramps (max 10% increase per hour)

rollout_plan:
Phase A - Internal canary: 100% internal team traffic; validate synthetic tests and manual review (24h)
Phase B - External opt-in: 5% of production traffic via feature flag for friendly customers (48h)
Phase C - Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with minimum observation windows (30m, 1h, 3h, 6h respectively)
Progression criteria: during each window, p95 < target * 1.1, error-rate < baseline + 0.5%, and error-budget burn-rate < 1.2
Abort/rollback criteria: immediate rollback if p99 exceeds target by > 2x for >5 minutes or availability drops below target - 0.2% over a 15m window
Traffic-shaping actions when gate fails: shed low-priority routes, redirect to model-fallback variant, or scale dedicated pool by burst capacity policy
Final signoff: PM + Eng on-call + SRE must approve 100% promotion and close rollout ticket

monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: per-route and per-model p50/p95/p99, availability, error-rate, and error-budget burn-rate
Alerts: SLO burn-rate > 4 (P0), availability drop > 0.1% vs target (P0), sustained p95 degradation meeting rollback criteria (P1)
Synthetic checks: run hourly; failures count toward gate evaluation and pipeline block
Audit logs: every automated gate decision must be recorded with telemetry snapshot and reason code

acceptance_criteria:
AC1: Programmatic SLO definitions exist in config store and are versioned alongside runtime release manifests
AC2: CI pipeline runs synthetic/regression traffic for all request classes and emits gate-pass/gate-fail signals
AC3: Console shows per-release rollout UI with gate status and has ability to manually pause/resume; automated rollback triggers observed in canary test runs
AC4: On-call runbooks and escalation flows published; PagerDuty policy created and validated by SREs
AC5: No user-facing incidents during a 7-day canary across opt-in customers for at least two independent releases before full rollout is enabled for new model variants
AC6: QA and SRE sign-off recorded in the release ticket before 100% promotion

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Telemetry blind spots (e.g., client-side latencies not captured) -> Mitigation: add synthetic client-based probes and require SDK timing headers
Risk: Canary sample not representative of traffic distribution -> Mitigation: use stratified sampling by tenant size and request mix for opt-in phase
Risk: Automated rollback cascades causing oscillation -> Mitigation: impose cooldown window and backoff policy before reattempt
Risk: Increased false positives from noisy p99 metrics -> Mitigation: require corroborating signals (error-rate or availability) before automatic rollback

decisions:
D1: Use request-class conditional SLOs rather than per-route only; simpler to map to client intent and test harness
D2: 30-day rolling window chosen for availability because it aligns with customer expectations and billing cycles
D3: Use burn-rate thresholds (short-term 1h and medium-term 3h) to detect rapid regressions without blocking minor oscillations
D4: Automated rollback will revert to the previous stable model variant and notify the on-call channel
